class.name: HDWIOneWireResource
class.brief_description: Virtual 1-Wire sensor exposed through the kernel's sysfs interface - e.g. a DS18B20 temperature sensor.
class.description:
Models one 1-Wire slave the FSW reads through sysfs. Most actions are read-only and the resource is device-agnostic: when the FSW opens a sysfs attribute, this resource emits [signal on_onewire_read] with an action telling GDScript [i]which[/i] attribute was opened, GDScript fills [member read_buffer] with the bytes that file should contain, and the buffer is shipped back verbatim. The read actions correspond to the sysfs files: [constant ONEWIRE_READ_TEMPERATURE] - the [code]temperature[/code] file (millidegrees as ASCII, e.g. [code]"21500
"[/code] = 21.5 C). [constant ONEWIRE_READ_SLAVE] - the [code]w1_slave[/code] file (raw scratchpad bytes plus a CRC line ending in [code]t=21500[/code]). [constant ONEWIRE_READ_RAW] - the generic [code]rw[/code] raw byte channel. [constant ONEWIRE_READ_RESOLUTION] - the [code]resolution[/code] file (ASCII digit 9-12). [member read_buffer] is pre-filled from [member resolution] before [signal on_onewire_read] fires, so this one works with no wiring at all unless you want to override it. [constant ONEWIRE_WRITE_RESOLUTION] is the one write action: the FSW wrote the [code]resolution[/code] file. The resource parses the ASCII payload, clamps to 9-12 (out-of-range writes are dropped, keeping the previous value), stores it in [member resolution], and emits [signal on_onewire_resolution_changed]. Unlike every other 1-Wire action this one is request/reply - the kernel thread blocks waiting for the ack, so the resource always sends one (even when the write was rejected) with no GDScript involvement required. [b]How to interface[/b] [olist] [*]Set [member sensor_index] - the kernel assigns indices by position in the sync body, so this must match that position (the registry emits sensors in [member sensor_index] order to keep them in sync). Set [member device_name] to the ROM id string. [*]Call [method HDWIResource.init] to register the sensor. [*]Connect [signal on_onewire_read]; in the handler, branch on the action and fill [member read_buffer] in the format that sysfs file expects. Not needed for [constant ONEWIRE_READ_RESOLUTION] unless overriding the default. [*]Connect [signal HDWIResource.on_send] to forward the response to the kernel socket. [*]Optionally connect [signal on_onewire_resolution_changed] to react when the FSW changes resolution (e.g. retune a conversion-time or noise model); [member resolution] is updated regardless of whether anything is connected. [/olist] [b]Example - a DS18B20 at 21.5 C[/b] [codeblock] var sensor = HDWIOneWireResource.new() sensor.device_name = "28-00000a1b2c3d" sensor.sensor_index = 0 sensor.init()
sensor.on_onewire_read.connect(_on_read) sensor.on_send.connect(_write_to_kernel_socket)
func _on_read(sensor_index, action): match action: HDWIOneWireResource.ONEWIRE_READ_TEMPERATURE: sensor.read_buffer = "21500
".to_utf8_buffer() HDWIOneWireResource.ONEWIRE_READ_SLAVE: sensor.read_buffer = "a1 01 4b 46 7f ff 0c 10 1c : crc=1c YES
a1 01 ... t=21500
".to_utf8_buffer() _: sensor.read_buffer = PackedByteArray() [/codeblock]

method.name: handle_onewire_read
method.description: Internal. Emits [signal on_onewire_read] (synchronous, so GDScript can fill [member read_buffer]), then frames the buffer and emits [signal HDWIResource.on_send]. Invoked by [method HDWIResource.dispatch_action] for any read action; for [constant ONEWIRE_READ_RESOLUTION] the dispatcher pre-fills [member read_buffer] from [member resolution] first.

method.name: handle_onewire_write_resolution
method.description: Internal. Parses the ASCII bytes the FSW wrote to the [code]resolution[/code] sysfs file; values outside 9-12 are dropped, keeping the previous [member resolution]. On acceptance, stores it in [member resolution] and emits [signal on_onewire_resolution_changed]. Always sends a data-less ack afterward regardless of acceptance - the kernel thread blocks on this reply, unlike [code]UART_WRITE[/code]. Invoked by [method HDWIResource.dispatch_action] for [constant ONEWIRE_WRITE_RESOLUTION].

method.name: get_group_type_representation
method.description: Builds the 1-Wire section of the [code]CMD_SYNCH[/code] registration body: [code][type][count][/code] followed by each sensor's 32-byte name, emitted in [member sensor_index] order so kernel-assigned indices line up.

method.name: lookup_onewire_device_id
method.description: Returns the 0-based registry slot of the sensor with the given [member sensor_index], or [code]-1[/code] if none is registered.

members.member: Natural identifier on the wire (inner 1-Wire header [code]sensor_index[/code]). Must match the position the kernel assigns during sync; registration is emitted in this order to guarantee that.

Raw response bytes for the current read. Fill this inside the [signal on_onewire_read] handler in the format that matches the requested action. Shipped verbatim - no transformation is applied. Pre-filled from [member resolution] before [signal on_onewire_read] fires for [constant ONEWIRE_READ_RESOLUTION].

Bit resolution (9-12) the FSW last set via the [code]resolution[/code] sysfs file. Source of truth for [constant ONEWIRE_READ_RESOLUTION] replies; [constant ONEWIRE_WRITE_RESOLUTION] writes update it directly. Defaults to the DS18B20 power-on default of 12 bits. Settable from GDScript at any time, e.g. to seed an initial value.

signal.name: on_onewire_read
signal.description: Emitted when the FSW reads a sysfs attribute on this sensor. [param action] is one of [constant ONEWIRE_READ_TEMPERATURE], [constant ONEWIRE_READ_SLAVE], [constant ONEWIRE_READ_RAW], [constant ONEWIRE_READ_RESOLUTION]; fill [member read_buffer] accordingly before the handler returns. For [constant ONEWIRE_READ_RESOLUTION] this is already pre-filled with [member resolution] formatted as ASCII - only connect if you need to override it.

signal.name: on_onewire_resolution_changed
signal.description: Emitted after the FSW writes a valid (9-12) value to the [code]resolution[/code] sysfs file and [member resolution] has been updated. Connect this only if something else needs to react to the change (e.g. a conversion-time or noise model keyed on bit resolution); [member resolution] itself is always kept current regardless of whether anything is connected.

constants.constant: The FSW opened the [code]temperature[/code] sysfs file; respond with millidegrees as ASCII (e.g. [code]"21500\n"[/code]).
The FSW opened the [code]w1_slave[/code] sysfs file; respond with the raw scratchpad bytes plus the CRC/[code]t=[/code] line.
The FSW opened the generic [code]rw[/code] raw channel; respond with raw bytes.

The FSW opened the [code]resolution[/code] sysfs file for reading; respond with the current bit resolution as ASCII (e.g. [code]"12\n"[/code]). [member read_buffer] is already pre-filled with this by the time [signal on_onewire_read] fires.

The FSW wrote a new bit resolution (9-12 ASCII) to the [code]resolution[/code] sysfs file. High bit (0x80) marks the write direction. Handled entirely internally: [member resolution] is updated (if valid) and an ack is always sent back - the kernel thread blocks on it. No GDScript wiring is required; connect [signal on_onewire_resolution_changed] only to react to the change.
